problems.location: Learning objectives; Concepts 1, 2, 7 and 8
problems.lesson_text: Explain how cultural, biological, and motivational processes—including brain plasticity, executive function, reconstructive memory, self-regulation, goal orientations, and stereotype threat—shape individual learning trajectories across the life span.
problems.source_text: Focus primarily on the slides, with the other two sources being additional information to fill in any gaps or as “fun facts”.
problems.reason: Four of the eight concepts and two of the four objectives come only from How People Learn II, so the lesson is built mainly on a supporting source and not on the slides.

problems.location: Concept 6: Learner Agency, Transparency, and Equity in AI-Mediated Systems / block 2
problems.lesson_text: Penalizes unconventional thinkers and reinforces historical bias in hiring or admissions.
problems.source_text: Fast can be useful. But scoring wants neat categories, and one rubric for everybody leaves little room for the things that make a person interesting.
problems.reason: The claim that automated judging reinforces historical bias in hiring or admissions is not in any source.

problems.location: Concept 6: Learner Agency, Transparency, and Equity in AI-Mediated Systems / block 2
problems.lesson_text: Accumulates permanent behavioral or linguistic records that can trigger disproportionate discipline.
problems.source_text: It can give peace of mind on one side of the screen. On the other side, it’s a record.
problems.reason: The sources say monitoring creates a record, but nothing about chilling effects or disproportionate discipline.

problems.location: Concept 6: Learner Agency, Transparency, and Equity in AI-Mediated Systems / block 3
problems.lesson_text: repetitive drill-and-practice, online benchmark testing, and automated monitoring
problems.source_text: children attending schools in less-privileged communities are more likely to use technology for drill-and-practice and for taking online benchmark assessments
problems.reason: The lesson adds automated monitoring to a research finding that names only drill-and-practice and online benchmark assessments.

problems.location: Concept 3: Situated Learning and the Six-Touchpoint Learning Ecosystem / block 3
problems.lesson_text: students bring home-based funds of knowledge
problems.reason: Funds of knowledge is used here but is not explained until Concept 7.

problems.location: Concept 2: Cultural Context, Motivation, and Identity in Learning / block 2
problems.lesson_text: Expectancy-Value Theory
problems.reason: The mind map lists Expectancy-Value Theory, Situational & Personal Interest and Self-Efficacy, but the lesson never defines them, and Exercise 2.1 then asks students to predict changes in self-efficacy.

problems.location: Concept 4: AI as Connective Tissue in Human-Centered Learning Ecosystems / block 3
problems.lesson_text: Supports collaborative inquiry, trialogues, and flipped discussions where teachers coach problem solving
problems.reason: Trialogues and flipped discussions are used as examples but are never explained.

problems.location: Concept 4: AI as Connective Tissue in Human-Centered Learning Ecosystems / block 2
problems.lesson_text: provided it bridges back to human coaching and a supportive transfer climate
problems.reason: Transfer climate, Knowledge Forum and WISE are named on this card but never explained, so the reader cannot follow the point.

problems.location: Concept 4: AI as Connective Tissue in Human-Centered Learning Ecosystems / block 1
problems.lesson_text: In reality, learning in the flow of work means learning *through real work, with other people*
problems.reason: This repeats the explanation of learning in the flow of work that Concept 3 block 1 already gave, without pointing back to it.

problems.location: Concept 6: Learner Agency, Transparency, and Equity in AI-Mediated Systems / blocks 1-2
problems.lesson_text: Automated grouping systems place students into reading tiers, intervention tracks, or talent pools based on algorithmic thresholds.
problems.reason: Concept 6 explains Choosing, Judging, Watching and Sorting again, with the same check-in questions as the Concept 5 table, instead of building on them.

problems.location: Concept 8: Designing Aligned Assessment and Technology-Integrated Environments / block 3
problems.lesson_text: Learners in under-resourced settings are disproportionately assigned drill-and-practice software, whereas affluent peers use simulations and creative production tools.
problems.reason: This repeats the creation-versus-drill equity gap that Concept 6 block 3 already explained in full.

problems.location: Concept 1: Biological and Cognitive Foundations of Learning Across the Life Span / block 1
problems.lesson_text: ask whether it exercises and tunes these adaptive neural networks—or bypasses the effortful processing required to strengthen them
problems.reason: The lesson jumps from neural mechanisms to judging digital tools, without saying that effortful processing drives tuning or how a leader could tell.

problems.location: Concept 2: Cultural Context, Motivation, and Identity in Learning / block 1
problems.lesson_text: The interplay of *will* (motivation and curiosity), *skill* (learning strategies), and *metacognitive control*
problems.reason: Metacognition, self-regulated learning and Self-Determination Theory are defined only in general terms, with no concrete case of a learner using them.

problems.location: Concept 8: Designing Aligned Assessment and Technology-Integrated Environments / block 1
problems.lesson_text: designers begin with the **claim space** (exactly what knowledge and skills learners should demonstrate), then specify the **evidence** required to support those claims, and finally design **tasks** that reliably elicit that evidence.
problems.reason: Evidence-Centered Design (ECD) is new to most leaders but is explained only in the abstract, with no worked claim, evidence and task.

problems.location: Concept 5: The Spectrum of Visible and Invisible AI in Education / block 3
problems.lesson_text: Background Decision Systems (Judging, Watching, Sorting)
problems.reason: The card's image is an empty, dark school hallway, which shows nothing about scoring, monitoring or grouping learners.

problems.location: Concept 8: Designing Aligned Assessment and Technology-Integrated Environments / block 3
problems.lesson_text: Reduce extraneous cognitive load by excluding irrelevant graphics or sounds (Coherence)
problems.reason: The image for Mayer's principles is a busy 3D web page with floating emojis and hearts, which shows the opposite of the coherence principle the card teaches.

problems.location: Concept 2: Cultural Context, Motivation, and Identity in Learning / block 4
problems.lesson_text: Stereotype Threat
problems.reason: The stereotype threat card shows a stock photo of a teacher at a laptop, which has nothing to do with the idea.

problems.location: Concept 5: The Spectrum of Visible and Invisible AI in Education / block 4
problems.lesson_text: link: Curating & Filtering AI -> Judging
problems.reason: The mind map puts the nine forms in four groups (Choosing with Judging), while block 3 uses three zones (Choosing in the middle) and block 5 puts Choosing with the invisible systems, so students get conflicting groupings.

problems.location: Concept 8: Designing Aligned Assessment and Technology-Integrated Environments
problems.lesson_text: Designing Aligned Assessment and Technology-Integrated Environments
problems.reason: One concept holds two large, separate topics, assessment design and technology design (affordances, multimedia, UDL, digital inclusion, implementation), with little to tie them together.

problems.location: Concept 1: Biological and Cognitive Foundations of Learning Across the Life Span / block 2
problems.lesson_text: Even very low blood-lead levels reduce reading, writing, and IQ scores, underscoring the importance of safe physical learning environments.
problems.reason: In a lesson on AI learning ecosystems, a whole block goes to nutrition, sleep and lead, while the core mapping activity and thinking routine get one sentence or nothing.

problems.location: Concept 1: Biological and Cognitive Foundations of Learning Across the Life Span / block 3
problems.lesson_text: Holds information in mind, inhibits premature responses, and sustains or shifts attention toward goals.
problems.reason: Executive function is named in learning objective 3, but no exercise tests it, even though Exercise 1.2's title promises it.

problems.location: Exercise 1.2: Reconstructive memory, environmental retrieval cues, and executive function in instructional contexts / block 4
problems.lesson_text: correct alternative: multiple spaced retrieval opportunities and active practice are needed for durable long-term memory.
problems.reason: The answer depends on spaced practice and retrieval practice, which are not taught until Concept 7.

problems.location: Exercise 5.2: Distinguishing intentional learner-chosen AI tools from background choosing, judging, watching, and sorting systems / block 2
problems.lesson_text: What is the term for AI that groups learners for downstream actions, such as unlocking services or flagging at-risk students?
problems.reason: Students can answer by copying the Sorting row of the Concept 5 table, while the objective asks them to classify and evaluate.

problems.location: Exercise 8.2: Aligning technology affordances, multimedia principles, and Universal Design for Learning in a systems implementation / block 2
problems.lesson_text: What is the three-part structure of evidence-centered design for assessment?
problems.reason: The question only asks students to recall the three parts, while the objective asks them to design assessments.

problems.location: Exercise 1.1: Lifelong neural plasticity, synaptic pruning, and compensatory recruitment in adult and K-12 learning / block 2
problems.lesson_text: Active explanation, so neural connections are reinforced
problems.reason: The question tests the value of explanation, a study strategy taught in Concept 7, not plasticity, pruning or recruitment, and Concept 1 never said explanation reinforces neural connections.

problems.location: Exercise 1.1: Lifelong neural plasticity, synaptic pruning, and compensatory recruitment in adult and K-12 learning / blocks 3-4
problems.lesson_text: begin using strategies that recruit both familiar and new problem-solving skills
problems.reason: The word recruit gives the answer away, and peer troubleshooting cannot show a brain-level mechanism, so the keyed answer Compensatory recruitment is not supported by the scenario.

problems.location: Exercise 5.1: Classifying visible and invisible forms of AI across the nine-category continuum in educational settings / block 2
problems.lesson_text: Background systems require learners to choose them, so agency is always high
problems.reason: The wrong options contradict the scenario outright (for example, All AI tools are equally visible), so only one option is believable.

problems.location: Exercise 5.1: Classifying visible and invisible forms of AI across the nine-category continuum in educational settings / block 4
problems.lesson_text: Invisible tools require employee action, so awareness is always high
problems.reason: The wrong options are clearly false from the scenario, so the question tests little.

problems.location: Exercise 4.1: Evaluating AI tools as connective tissue for joint attention, just-in-time support, and peer collaboration / block 3
problems.lesson_text: AI grades all lab reports, so teachers are not needed
problems.reason: In questions 1 to 3, the wrong options are extreme statements (all, unnecessary, bypassed) that the scenarios rule out, and only the right answer repeats the scenario's wording.

problems.location: Exercise 3.1: Structural versus surface differences and situated learning principles across contrasting learning ecosystems / block 3
problems.lesson_text: Assess Priya's autonomy in each
problems.reason: Priya's control is one of the structural differences the lesson taught, so this option is also a defensible first step next to the keyed answer.

problems.location: Exercise 6.2: Digital inclusion, unequal access to empowering technologies, and policy recommendations to adopt, adapt, or reject AI systems / block 3
problems.lesson_text: Identify how the system affects agency
problems.reason: Question 1 marks agency as the first step, but the question 5 rubric makes transparency step 1 and agency step 2, so the answer keys conflict.

problems.location: Concept 7: Evidence-Based Learning Strategies and Asset-Based Pedagogy / block 1
problems.lesson_text: Mixing different skills, problem types, or categories within a session introduces *desirable difficulties*
problems.source_text: when given the option, a majority of learners preferred to block their study
problems.reason: The lesson never says that interleaved and spaced practice feel harder and can lower short-term scores, so leaders may wrongly judge these methods as failing.
